about: Every requirement between a person and a Wisconsin K-12 job, one entry each. 'kind' is credential (a license or degree; Eligibility adds it when a job needs it and the person lacks it) or step (onboarding everyone in 'roles' goes through). 'blocks' says what waits on it: apply (don't apply before it), first_day (apply now; you can't start until it's done) or none. 'time' is in days, 'cost' in US dollars with who pays. 'collect' is what the checklist stores: done, date, or date+expiry; never a document. 'never' is shown as a warning. 'conflict' marks facts sources disagree on; the site shows it as 'confirm with the employer'. Re-check entries older than 120 days (verified_on); the settings screen lists them. Guidance only, not legal advice.

sub_training.title: DPI-approved substitute teacher training
sub_training.why: Wisconsin's degree-path substitute permit needs an approved training course (PI 34.032). A bachelor's degree doesn't exempt you.

time.label: About 8 hours online, or 1–2 days in person

cost.label: Free through EDUStaff, Kelly Education or a district; $40–$80 elsewhere

how: Pick one course. If you'll apply to EDUStaff or a district that trains its own subs, theirs is free.
Save the completion certificate as a PDF. DPI asks for it in your permit application.
sub_training.proof: Completion certificate (or form PI-1633 from the district)

valid.note: Doesn't expire; used once for the permit application

fingerprints.title: Fingerprints for DPI (Fieldprint)
fingerprints.why: DPI needs fingerprints if you've lived, worked or studied outside Wisconsin (another state, a US territory, Canada or Great Britain) since your last DPI fingerprint submission.

time.label: Book an appointment; results add about 2–4 weeks to DPI's processing

how: Book through Fieldprint with code FPWIDPITeach and bring two forms of ID to the appointment.
Do this before or alongside your DPI application; DPI waits for the prints.

valid.note: Needed again only if you live, work or study outside Wisconsin later

fingerprints.conflict: DPI doesn't publish Fieldprint's price; agencies quote $39–$40.

sub_permit.title: Three-Year Short-Term Substitute Teacher Permit
sub_permit.why: A Wisconsin public school can't put you in a classroom as a substitute teacher without a DPI license or permit (PI 34.032).

time.label: DPI takes about 6–8 weeks (8–12 with fingerprints)

cost.label: $135, credit card only, not refunded if denied

how: In ELO choose 1-Teacher → S-Teacher – Short Term Substitute License [T910] → Request Short-term Substitute License [1910].
Attach your official transcript and training certificate (PDF, Word or JPG, 2 MB or less each).
Answer the 14 Conduct & Competency questions in one sitting (no save; it times out after 30 minutes) and pay by Mastercard, Visa or Discover credit card.
Apply to employers the same week. Their applications don't wait on the permit; only your first day does.
ELO is offline Wednesdays 10 pm to Thursdays 2 am.
sub_permit.proof: Permit number from ELO; employers check it on DPI's public license lookup

valid.note: Any subject and grade, up to 45 consecutive days in one assignment. Renew in ELO.

long_term_license.title: Five-Year Long-Term Substitute License
long_term_license.why: Assignments longer than 45 consecutive days need a license for the assignment. This license is the route for people who finished an educator-preparation program, including retired teachers whose license lapsed (PI 34.033).

time.label: About 6–8 weeks; 8–12 if you were licensed out of state

cost.label: $135; $190 if your license is from another state

how: Apply in ELO with your transcript and proof you completed an approved educator-preparation program (or your out-of-state license).
Answer the Conduct & Competency questions and pay by credit card.

valid.note: Long-term assignments in your license area; short-term (45 days or less) outside it

long_term_license.conflict: Copies of PI 34.033 show both a 2-year and a 5-year term; DPI's page calls it the Five-Year Substitute License.

teaching_license.title: Wisconsin teaching license in the job's subject and grades
teaching_license.why: Public schools must place a teacher licensed for the subject and grade level (PI 34). Every Wisconsin teaching license needs a bachelor's degree.

time.label: 6–8 weeks once you qualify; an educator-preparation program takes 1–2 years

how: Licensed in another state: apply in ELO for the matching Wisconsin license (Tier II) with your license and transcripts.
Bachelor's degree but no license: a district that wants to hire you can request a One-Year License with Stipulations while you enroll in an educator-preparation program.
No bachelor's yet: finish one; an education degree includes the license program.

valid.note: Tier II license; renew through ELO

stipulations.title: One-Year License with Stipulations (district requests it)
stipulations.why: Lets a district, charter, private school or CESA that couldn't find a fully licensed teacher hire someone with a bachelor's degree while they complete an educator-preparation program. The employer files the request (form PI-1624-LWS1).

time.label: After the district offers the job and requests it; about 6–8 weeks

cost.label: $140, plus enrollment in an educator-preparation program

how: Ask the district during the interview whether it will request this license for you.
Enroll in an approved educator-preparation program; the district and the program both sign off in ELO.

valid.note: Renewable while you make progress in the program

sepa_license.title: Special Education Program Aide license
sepa_license.why: Aides in public-school special-education programs need this DPI license unless they hold another DPI license.

time.label: About 4–8 weeks

how: Apply in ELO, answer the Conduct & Competency questions and pay by credit card.
Apply to the district at the same time; ask whether it starts the request for you.
sepa_license.conflict: DPI's current page has the aide apply in ELO; an older DPI bulletin says the district requests it.

title1_para.title: Title I paraprofessional standard (48 credits, associate degree or ParaPro test)
title1_para.why: Federal law (ESSA) requires paraprofessionals in Title I schoolwide buildings, or working with Title I students, to have 48 college credits, an associate degree, or a passing score on an approved assessment.

time.label: Book and take the test in 1–4 weeks

cost.label: Test fee set by the testing center; some districts pay it

how: Ask the school whether the job is in a Title I building or program.
If you have 48 credits or an associate degree, your transcript covers it. Otherwise ask the district which test it accepts (ParaPro, WorkKeys or a portfolio).
title1_para.proof: Transcript, or the test score report
title1_para.conflict: Each district decides which assessment and passing score it accepts.

associate_degree.title: Associate degree (or enroll in an educator-preparation program)
associate_degree.why: DPI's substitute permit needs an associate degree or higher, or enrollment in a Wisconsin educator-preparation program at junior standing, age 20 or older.

time.label: About 2 years full time

cost.label: Tuition varies; financial aid and employer programs can cover it

how: Wisconsin technical colleges offer an associate degree in Foundations of Teacher Education that also counts toward a bachelor's.
Meanwhile you can work as an aide: most aide jobs need only a high-school diploma.

bachelor_degree.title: Bachelor's degree
bachelor_degree.why: Every Wisconsin teaching license, and some employers' substitute jobs (Milwaukee Public Schools, Racine building subs), need a bachelor's degree.

time.label: 2–4 years

how: An education degree from a Wisconsin educator-preparation program includes the license.

high_school.title: High-school diploma or GED/HSED
high_school.why: Aide jobs, including Title I paraprofessional jobs, start from a high-school diploma or equivalent.

time.label: A few months to a year for a GED/HSED

how: Adult-education centers and technical colleges offer free GED/HSED preparation.

transcript.title: Order an official transcript
transcript.why: DPI's application and most employers ask for an official transcript of your highest degree.

time.label: Electronic transcripts arrive in 1–3 days; paper ones take longer

where.label: Your college's registrar (most use Parchment or the National Student Clearinghouse)

how: Order an electronic PDF you can attach more than once, if your college offers one.
transcript.proof: Transcript PDF, kept on your own device
transcript.never: Give it to DPI and employers directly; this site never stores documents.

references.title: Line up references
references.why: Employers and agencies contact references before hiring; Milwaukee Public Schools asks for three letters under 3 years old.

time.label: Ask early; people take a week or two

how: Ask three people who've seen you work with children or at work: a supervisor, a teacher you've worked with, a coach or volunteer coordinator.
Ask once for a letter you can reuse with every employer.
Self-employed? Don't list your own business: the reference form comes back to you. Name a client or a colleague instead.
references.proof: Names and contact details you've checked with each person

valid.note: Letters older than 3 years may not be accepted

interview.title: Interview, workshop or orientation
interview.why: Every employer and agency meets you before hiring. Agency workshops count as an interview.

time.label: Usually scheduled within 2 weeks of applying; 1–2 hours

how: Bring anything the employer asked you to print and sign, and the original ID documents you'll use for Form I-9.
Don't have your permit or TB screening yet? Go anyway; ask what can follow later.

employer_background.title: Employer background check consent
employer_background.why: Employers check criminal records before hiring school staff. When they use a screening company, federal law (FCRA) requires your written consent first.

time.label: 15 minutes to consent; results in a few days

cost.label: Usually paid by the employer; some agencies charge a one-time fee

where.label: Wisconsin DOJ record check (what employers see)

how: Watch for an email from the employer or its screening company and finish the consent form within the deadline it gives (often 24–48 hours).
This site never asks about arrests or convictions: under Wis. Stat. 111.335 employers can't ask about arrests, and can use a conviction only if it relates substantially to the job.
employer_background.proof: Confirmation email from the screening company

valid.note: Some agencies repeat it every 5 years

employer_background.never: Enter your Social Security number only on the screening company's own secure form, never by email.

tb_screen.title: Physical exam with TB risk questionnaire
tb_screen.why: Wis. Stat. 118.25 makes a physical exam, including a TB risk assessment, a condition of employment for school staff who work with children. A TB test is needed only if the questionnaire shows a risk.

time.label: One clinic visit; 2–3 more days if a skin test is needed

cost.label: The school board pays under 118.25; agencies may ask you to pay and reimburse

how: Ask the employer which forms it uses, then take them to your doctor or an urgent-care clinic.
Keep the receipt; ask the employer about reimbursement.
tb_screen.proof: The signed form, given to the employer only

valid.note: Some employers and agencies want it dated within 90 days of hire

tb_screen.never: Medical results go to the employer only. Never upload or email them here.
tb_screen.conflict: The statute covers school-board employees; agency-employed staff follow the agency's contract with the district.

mandated_reporter.title: Mandated reporter training (child abuse and neglect)
mandated_reporter.why: Wis. Stat. 118.07(5): every school employee completes it within 6 months of hire, then every 5 years.

time.label: About 1 hour online

how: Take DPI's free online course and save the certificate. Already done it for another district? It still counts; keep the certificate.

valid.note: Within 6 months of hire, then every 5 years

school_violence.title: Reporting threats of school violence training
school_violence.why: 2017 Wisconsin Act 143: school employees report threats of school violence and are trained on the same schedule as mandated reporting.

time.label: Under an hour online

how: Take it right after the mandated reporter course and save the certificate.

valid.note: Within 6 months of hire, then every 5 years

grooming_boundaries.title: Grooming and personal boundaries training (Act 89)
grooming_boundaries.why: Wis. Stat. 118.07(7), from 2025 Wisconsin Acts 88 and 89: public, private and charter school employees complete it every year starting in 2026-27.

time.label: About 20 minutes online

where.label: DPI module: Grooming and Personal Boundaries

how: Watch the module, answer the questions and enter your email at the end to get the completion confirmation.
Already done it this school year for another district, or as a school volunteer or chaperone? It's the same DPI module: send that certificate instead of retaking it.

bloodborne.title: Bloodborne pathogens training
bloodborne.why: OSHA 29 CFR 1910.1030: staff who may contact blood (nurses, special-education staff, coaches, first-aid duty) are trained when assigned, then yearly.

time.label: Under an hour; the employer assigns it

how: The employer or agency assigns it in its onboarding portal.

i9.title: Form I-9: show proof you can work in the US
i9.why: Federal law: you complete section 1 by your first day; the employer checks your original documents within 3 business days. The employer can't tell you which acceptable documents to bring.

time.label: 10 minutes at orientation

how: Choose documents from USCIS's list (for example a passport, or a driver's license plus a Social Security card) and bring the originals.
i9.proof: Nothing to keep; the employer files it
i9.never: Show ID documents in person. Never email or upload them, here or anywhere else.

tax_forms.title: Tax forms W-4 and WT-4
tax_forms.why: Every new hire gives the employer a federal W-4 and Wisconsin's WT-4 (Wis. Admin. Code Tax 2.92).

time.label: 15 minutes in the employer's payroll portal

how: Fill them in the employer's own payroll system after you're hired.
tax_forms.never: Your Social Security number goes only into the employer's payroll system.

direct_deposit.title: Choose how you're paid
direct_deposit.why: Without bank details, some agencies pay onto a paycard by default.

time.label: 5 minutes

how: Enter bank details in the employer's payroll portal, or accept the paycard.
direct_deposit.never: Bank details go only into the employer's payroll portal.

absence_system.title: Set up the substitute scheduling app
absence_system.why: Daily substitute jobs aren't posted publicly: once you're active, they're offered through the employer's absence system (usually Frontline or Red Rover).

time.label: 15 minutes

how: Use the login the employer sends you, set your schools, grades and days, and turn on notifications.

renewal.title: Calendar your license renewal
renewal.why: A substitute permit lasts 3 years and most licenses 5; working on an expired one isn't allowed.

time.label: 2 minutes

how: Add a reminder 3 months before the expiry date and renew in ELO.

drug_test.title: Drug and alcohol test
drug_test.why: Milwaukee Public Schools tests new substitutes before they start.

time.label: One clinic visit; MPS schedules it

how: Wait for MPS to send the clinic details after your interview.

edustaff.note: One EDUStaff application covers every district it serves. Expect: online application (about 2 hours, can be saved), a 2-hour in-person workshop that counts as an interview, the aINSIGHT background-check consent, online modules (Active Shooter, Bloodborne Pathogens, FERPA, Seclusion & Restraint, Title IX), TB paperwork and the DPI grooming module.

kelly.note: Kelly Education: apply online, a pre-screen, a virtual group interview, a free classroom-management course (ClassSmarts), background check with fingerprints, then a paid orientation.
